objects.definition:
typedef struct ZSTD_CCtx_s ZSTD_CCtx;
typedef ZSTD_CCtx ZSTD_CStream;  /**< CCtx and CStream are now effectively same object (>= v1.3.0) */
objects.description: Opaque compression context for zstd. Allocate with ZSTD_createCCtx()/ZSTD_createCStream() and free with corresponding free functions. ZSTD_CStream is an alias used for streaming APIs; both refer to the same underlying opaque type.

objects.definition:
typedef struct ZSTD_DCtx_s ZSTD_DCtx;
typedef ZSTD_DCtx ZSTD_DStream;  /**< DCtx and DStream are now effectively same object (>= v1.3.0) */
objects.description: Opaque decompression context for zstd. Allocate with ZSTD_createDCtx()/ZSTD_createDStream() and free with corresponding free functions. ZSTD_DStream is an alias used for streaming APIs; both refer to the same underlying opaque type.
Opaque digested compression dictionary. Create from raw dict bytes once, then reuse across compressions for faster startup. Thread-safe for concurrent read-only use.
Opaque digested decompression dictionary. Create from raw dict bytes to avoid per-call setup cost. Used by decompression contexts.
By-value POD describing an input buffer for streaming APIs. Holds pointer, total size, and current position updated by API calls.
By-value POD describing an output buffer for streaming APIs. Holds pointer, total size, and current write position updated by API calls.
Small struct returned by parameter-bounds query functions containing an error status and inclusive lower/upper bounds for a parameter.

objects.description: Enumeration of compressor parameters set/get via advanced API. Some values correspond to experimental controls gated by ZSTD_STATIC_LINKING_ONLY.
Directive for resetting a CCtx/DCtx: reset session state, parameters, or both.
Enumeration of decompressor parameters set/get via advanced API. Some entries are experimental-only.
End directive for streaming compression to continue, flush, or end a frame.

functions.name: ZSTD_versionNumber
functions.description: Returns the runtime zstd library version as (MAJOR*100*100 + MINOR*100 + RELEASE). Use to check the linked library version at runtime.

functions.name: ZSTD_versionString
functions.description: Returns the runtime zstd library version string, e.g. "1.5.7". Requires v1.3.0+.

functions.name: ZSTD_compress
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compress(void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, int compressionLevel);
functions.description: Compresses src into a single zstd frame into an already-allocated dst buffer at the given compression level. Providing dstCapacity >= ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize) guarantees enough space for compression.
requirements: dstCapacity must be large enough to contain the compressed frame; using ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize) eliminates capacity failures.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_decompress
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompress(void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t compressedSize);
functions.description: Decompresses one or more concatenated zstd/skippable frames from src into dst. The result is the concatenation of all decoded frames. dstCapacity is an upper bound on the total decompressed size.
requirements: compressedSize must be the exact size of the provided compressed/skippable frames sequence.
dstCapacity must be at least as large as the total decompressed output; if unknown, prefer streaming decompression.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_getFrameContentSize
functions.signature: unsigned long long ZSTD_getFrameContentSize(const void* src, size_t srcSize);
functions.description: Parses a zstd frame header starting at src and returns the decompressed content size if known, ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN if not determinable, or ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_ERROR on error. A return of 0 means a valid but empty frame (also returned for skippable frames).
requirements: src must point to the start of a zstd-encoded frame.
srcSize must be at least the frame header size (any size >= ZSTD_frameHeaderSize_max is sufficient).
Always validate that the returned size fits your application's limits, especially for untrusted inputs.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDecompressedSize
functions.signature: unsigned long long ZSTD_getDecompressedSize(const void* src, size_t srcSize);
functions.description: Obsolete in favor of ZSTD_getFrameContentSize(). Returns the decompressed size if known and not empty; otherwise returns 0. Blends empty, unknown, and error into 0.
requirements: Prefer ZSTD_getFrameContentSize() for distinct empty/unknown/error conditions.

functions.name: ZSTD_findFrameCompressedSize
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_findFrameCompressedSize(const void* src, size_t srcSize);
functions.description: Returns the compressed size of the first frame (zstd or skippable) starting at src, suitable for passing as srcSize to decompression. May scan through the frame to find its end. Returns an error code on invalid input.
requirements: src must point to the start of a zstd or skippable frame.
srcSize must be >= the size of the first frame; otherwise an error is returned.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressBound
functions.description: Returns the maximum compressed size for a worst-case single-pass compression of srcSize bytes. Can fail (return an error code) if srcSize >= ZSTD_MAX_INPUT_SIZE.
requirements: If srcSize >= ZSTD_MAX_INPUT_SIZE the function returns an error code; test with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_isError
functions.description: Returns 1 if result is a zstd error code, 0 otherwise. Use to check size_t-returning API results for errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_getErrorCode
functions.description: Converts a size_t function result into a ZSTD_ErrorCode that can be compared against zstd error enums.

functions.name: ZSTD_getErrorName
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for a size_t function result (error or success code).

functions.name: ZSTD_minCLevel
functions.description: Returns the minimum negative compression level allowed. Requires v1.4.0+.

functions.name: ZSTD_maxCLevel
functions.description: Returns the maximum compression level available.

functions.name: ZSTD_defaultCLevel
functions.description: Returns the default compression level (ZSTD_CLEVEL_DEFAULT). Requires v1.5.0+.

functions.name: ZSTD_createCCtx
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new compression context. Recommended to reuse across compressions for performance.

functions.name: ZSTD_freeCCtx
functions.description: Frees a compression context allocated by ZSTD_createCCtx(). Accepts NULL.
requirements: Pass a context obtained from ZSTD_createCCtx(); NULL is accepted.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressCCtx
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compressCCtx(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, int compressionLevel);
functions.description: Same as ZSTD_compress() but uses an explicit compression context. Mirrors ZSTD_compress() behavior and compresses at the provided compression level, ignoring other advanced parameters (any previously set advanced parameters are reset).
requirements: cctx must be a valid compression context.
dstCapacity should be >= ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize) to avoid capacity failures.
Advanced parameters previously set on cctx are ignored/reset; only compressionLevel applies.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_createDCtx
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new decompression context. Reuse across decompressions for performance.

functions.name: ZSTD_freeDCtx
functions.description: Frees a decompression context allocated by ZSTD_createDCtx(). Accepts NULL.
requirements: Pass a context obtained from ZSTD_createDCtx(); NULL is accepted.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_decompressDCtx
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompressDCtx(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize);
functions.description: Decompresses like ZSTD_decompress(), using an explicit decompression context. Compatible with sticky parameters set via the advanced API.
requirements: dctx must be a valid decompression context.
src must point to exactly one or more complete frames/skippable frames totaling srcSize bytes.
dstCapacity must be sufficient for the decompressed output; use streaming if unknown.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_cParam_getBounds
functions.description: Returns the inclusive lower and upper bounds for a compression parameter. The returned struct includes an error field that must be checked with ZSTD_isError().
requirements: Always test the returned .error field with ZSTD_isError() before using bounds.

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_setParameter
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_setParameter(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, ZSTD_cParameter param, int value);
functions.description: Sets a single compression parameter on a context. Values are clamped or error if out of bounds. Generally only allowed during frame initialization. In multithreaded mode (nbWorkers >= 1), a subset of parameters can be updated during compression and take effect for the next job after a flush.
requirements: Parameter values must be within bounds (query with ZSTD_cParam_getBounds()).

Setting parameters is generally only permitted before starting compression; in MT mode, compressionLevel, hashLog, chainLog, searchLog, minMatch, targetLength, and strategy can be updated during compression for the next job after a flush.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_setPledgedSrcSize
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_setPledgedSrcSize(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, unsigned long long pledgedSrcSize);
functions.description: Declares the total input size for the next frame. It is written to the frame header unless disabled, and is verified at end of frame. Valid only for the next frame, then reset to unknown.
requirements: pledgedSrcSize==0 means an empty frame; use ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN to mean unknown size.
This setting applies once to the next frame only; it is discarded after the frame.
When all input is provided in a single round (e.g., ZSTD_compress2 or immediately using ZSTD_compressStream2 with ZSTD_e_end), this value is overridden by srcSize.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_reset
functions.description: Resets a compression context. Can reset the session, parameters, or both. Resetting the session stops the current frame and readies the context for a new one; resetting parameters returns all parameters to defaults and removes references to dictionaries or external producers.
requirements: Resetting parameters is only allowed when no compression is ongoing; otherwise returns an error.
Resetting the session never fails; any buffered but unflushed data is discarded.

functions.name: ZSTD_compress2
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compress2(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize);
functions.description: Compresses using a context configured via the advanced API (ZSTD_CCtx_set*). Always starts a new frame and is blocking until completion. dstCapacity >= ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize) guarantees enough space (though other errors may occur).
requirements: cctx must have desired parameters set via ZSTD_CCtx_set*() prior to call.
dstCapacity should be >= ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize) to avoid capacity failures.
Starts a new frame; any unfinished previous frame state is forgotten.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_dParam_getBounds
functions.description: Returns the inclusive lower and upper bounds for a decompression parameter. The returned struct contains an error field to check with ZSTD_isError().
requirements: Always test the returned .error field with ZSTD_isError() before using bounds.

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_setParameter
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_DCtx_setParameter(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, ZSTD_dParameter param, int value);
functions.description: Sets a decompression parameter on a context. Values are clamped or error if out of bounds. Only allowed during frame initialization (before starting decompression).
requirements: Parameter values must be within bounds (query with ZSTD_dParam_getBounds()).
Must be called before starting decompression for a frame.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_reset
functions.description: Resets a decompression context. Session and parameters can be reset jointly or separately. Parameters can only be reset when no active frame is being decompressed.
requirements: Parameters can only be reset when no active frame is being decompressed.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_createCStream
functions.description: Allocates and returns a streaming compression object (alias of CCtx since v1.3.0).

functions.name: ZSTD_freeCStream
functions.description: Frees a streaming compression object. Accepts NULL.
requirements: Pass a context obtained from ZSTD_createCStream(); NULL is accepted.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressStream2
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compressStream2(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, ZSTD_outBuffer* output, ZSTD_inBuffer* input, ZSTD_EndDirective endOp);
functions.description: Streaming compression with control over the end directive. Updates input->pos/output->pos, guarantees they remain within size limits. Blocking when nbWorkers==0; non-blocking when nbWorkers>=1 except special first-call ZSTD_e_end case. Returns the minimum remaining data to flush or 0 when fully flushed (with ZSTD_e_flush/ZSTD_e_end), or an error.
requirements: output->pos must be <= output->size; input->pos must be <= input->size; both are updated by the function.
endOp must be a valid ZSTD_EndDirective.
When nbWorkers>=1, the call is non-blocking and may return >0 indicating data remains to flush; continue calling until it returns 0 for ZSTD_e_flush/ZSTD_e_end.
After an error, the cctx must be reset before reuse.
If the first call sets ZSTD_e_end and dstCapacity is sufficient, the function delegates to ZSTD_compress2() (blocking).

functions.name: ZSTD_CStreamInSize
functions.description: Returns the recommended input buffer size for streaming compression.

functions.name: ZSTD_CStreamOutSize
functions.description: Returns the recommended output buffer size for streaming compression. Guaranteed to flush at least one complete compressed block.

functions.name: ZSTD_initCStream
functions.description: Legacy streaming init helper. Equivalent to resetting the session, clearing any dictionary, and setting the compression level. Returns a code or error.
requirements: zcs must be a valid ZSTD_CStream.
This call clears any previously set dictionary.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressStream
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compressStream(ZSTD_CStream* zcs, ZSTD_outBuffer* output, ZSTD_inBuffer* input);
functions.description: Legacy streaming compression. Alternative to ZSTD_compressStream2(zcs, output, input, ZSTD_e_continue). Returns a hint for the next read size (if non-zero and not an error), unlike compressStream2 which returns bytes left to flush.
requirements: Update and respect input->pos <= size and output->pos <= size semantics.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_flushStream
functions.description: Legacy streaming helper. Equivalent to ZSTD_compressStream2(zcs, output, &emptyInput, ZSTD_e_flush). Returns 0 when fully flushed, >0 when more flushing is required, or an error.
requirements: Repeat calls until return value is 0 to fully flush.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_endStream
functions.description: Legacy streaming helper. Equivalent to ZSTD_compressStream2(zcs, output, &emptyInput, ZSTD_e_end). Returns 0 when frame completed and fully flushed, >0 when more flushing is required, or an error.
requirements: Repeat calls until return value is 0 to finish the frame.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_createDStream
functions.description: Allocates and returns a streaming decompression object (alias of DCtx since v1.3.0).

functions.name: ZSTD_freeDStream
functions.description: Frees a streaming decompression object. Accepts NULL.
requirements: Pass a context obtained from ZSTD_createDStream(); NULL is accepted.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_initDStream
functions.description: Initializes/resets the DStream for a new decompression operation. Equivalent to resetting the session and clearing any dictionary. Returns a recommended first input size.
requirements: zds must be a valid ZSTD_DStream.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_decompressStream
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompressStream(ZSTD_DStream* zds, ZSTD_outBuffer* output, ZSTD_inBuffer* input);
functions.description: Streaming decompression. Repeatedly call to consume input and produce output. Updates input->pos/output->pos. Returns 0 when the current frame is completely decoded and fully flushed; >0 hints next input size or indicates flushing remains; or an error.
requirements: Update and respect input->pos <= size and output->pos <= size semantics.
If output.pos == output.size and return > 0, call again to flush remaining data (possibly with no additional input).
After an error, the zds must be reset before reuse.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_DStreamInSize
functions.description: Returns the recommended input buffer size for streaming decompression.

functions.name: ZSTD_DStreamOutSize
functions.description: Returns the recommended output buffer size for streaming decompression. Guaranteed to flush at least one complete block in all circumstances.

functions.name: ZSTD_compress_usingDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compress_usingDict(ZSTD_CCtx* ctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, const void* dict, size_t dictSize, int compressionLevel);
functions.description: Compresses at an explicit compression level using a provided dictionary buffer or prefix. The dictionary is loaded each call (higher startup cost). If dict is NULL or dictSize < 8, no dictionary is used.
requirements: ctx must be a valid compression context.
If using a dictionary, dict must point to the dictionary buffer; loading incurs startup cost.
dstCapacity should be >= ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize) to avoid capacity failures.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_decompress_usingDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompress_usingDict(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, const void* dict, size_t dictSize);
functions.description: Decompresses using a provided dictionary. The dictionary must be identical to that used for compression. The dictionary is loaded each call (higher startup cost). If dict is NULL or dictSize < 8, no dictionary is used.
requirements: dctx must be a valid decompression context.
If a dictionary was used for compression, the identical dictionary must be provided.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_createCDict
functions.signature: ZSTD_CDict* ZSTD_createCDict(const void* dictBuffer, size_t dictSize, int compressionLevel);
functions.description: Digests a dictionary buffer into a reusable compression dictionary (CDict). Can be shared concurrently across threads (read-only). dictBuffer content is copied into the CDict; it may be freed after creation.
requirements: dictBuffer must point to the dictionary bytes to digest; it is copied internally.
A CDict may be created from an empty buffer to carry only the compressionLevel.

functions.name: ZSTD_freeCDict
functions.description: Frees a compression dictionary created by ZSTD_createCDict(). Accepts NULL.
requirements: Pass a dictionary obtained from ZSTD_createCDict(); NULL is accepted.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_compress_usingCDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compress_usingCDict(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, const ZSTD_CDict* cdict);
functions.description: Compresses using a pre-digested dictionary (CDict). Compression level and certain frame parameters are fixed by the CDict (dictID=yes, contentSize=yes, checksum=no). Recommended when the same dictionary is used multiple times.
requirements: cctx must be a valid compression context; cdict must be a valid CDict.
dstCapacity should be >= ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize) to avoid capacity failures.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_createDDict
functions.signature: ZSTD_DDict* ZSTD_createDDict(const void* dictBuffer, size_t dictSize);
functions.description: Digests a dictionary buffer into a reusable decompression dictionary (DDict). dictBuffer content is copied into the DDict; it may be freed after creation.
requirements: dictBuffer must point to the dictionary bytes to digest; it is copied internally.

functions.name: ZSTD_freeDDict
functions.description: Frees a decompression dictionary created by ZSTD_createDDict(). Accepts NULL.
requirements: Pass a dictionary obtained from ZSTD_createDDict(); NULL is accepted.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_decompress_usingDDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompress_usingDDict(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, const ZSTD_DDict* ddict);
functions.description: Decompresses using a pre-digested dictionary (DDict). Recommended when the same dictionary is used multiple times.
requirements: dctx must be a valid decompression context; ddict must be a valid DDict.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDictID_fromDict
functions.signature: unsigned ZSTD_getDictID_fromDict(const void* dict, size_t dictSize);
functions.description: Returns the dictID stored within a dictionary buffer. If 0, the dictionary is not conformant to the Zstandard spec (content-only) but can still be loaded.
requirements: dict must point to the dictionary buffer to inspect.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDictID_fromCDict
functions.description: Returns the dictID of the dictionary loaded into cdict. If 0, the dictionary is not conformant to the Zstandard spec or empty; non-conformant dictionaries can still be used as content-only.
requirements: cdict must be a valid CDict.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDictID_fromDDict
functions.description: Returns the dictID of the dictionary loaded into ddict. If 0, the dictionary is not conformant to the Zstandard spec or empty; non-conformant dictionaries can still be used as content-only.
requirements: ddict must be a valid DDict.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDictID_fromFrame
functions.signature: unsigned ZSTD_getDictID_fromFrame(const void* src, size_t srcSize);
functions.description: Returns the dictID required to decompress the frame at src. Returns 0 if it cannot be decoded (no dictionary required, dictID intentionally removed/non-conformant dict, srcSize too small, or not a zstd frame).
requirements: src must point to the start of a zstd frame; srcSize should be >= ZSTD_FRAMEHEADERSIZE_MAX to guarantee header decoding.
Use ZSTD_getFrameHeader() for more precise error diagnosis if needed.

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_loadDictionary
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_loadDictionary(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, const void* dict, size_t dictSize);
functions.description: Builds and sets an internal compression dictionary from dict content. Dictionary is sticky for future frames until changed or reset. Loading involves building tables and prevents changing compression parameters afterwards. Passing NULL or 0-size invalidates any previously loaded dictionary (no-dictionary mode).
requirements: dict content is copied internally; it may be freed after the call.
After loading, compression parameters can no longer be changed until reset.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_refCDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_refCDict(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, const ZSTD_CDict* cdict);
functions.description: References a prepared compression dictionary for all future frames. CDict parameters supersede CCtx parameters labeled as superseded-by-cdict. Referencing NULL returns to no-dictionary mode. Only one dictionary is managed at a time.
requirements: cdict is referenced (not copied) and must outlive its use in cctx.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_refPrefix
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_refPrefix(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, const void* prefix, size_t prefixSize);
functions.description: References a single-use prefix (raw content by default) for the next compressed frame. Tables are discarded at end of frame. Compatible with LDM. Referencing any prefix (including NULL) invalidates any previous prefix or dictionary.
requirements: prefix buffer is referenced and must outlive the compression; its content must remain unmodified during compression.
Ensure window size is large enough to reference the intended history if diffing large data.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_loadDictionary
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_DCtx_loadDictionary(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, const void* dict, size_t dictSize);
functions.description: Builds and sets an internal decompression dictionary for future frames. Dictionary remains active until invalidated or replaced. Loading involves building tables (non-negligible latency). Passing NULL or 0-size invalidates any previously loaded dictionary (no-dictionary mode).
requirements: dict content is copied internally; it may be freed after the call.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_refDDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_DCtx_refDDict(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, const ZSTD_DDict* ddict);
functions.description: References a prepared decompression dictionary for future frames. With ZSTD_d_refMultipleDDicts enabled, multiple references can be stored and selected by dictID at decompression time; otherwise only one dictionary is managed. Referencing NULL returns to no-dictionary mode.
requirements: ddict is referenced (not copied) and must outlive its use in dctx.
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_refPrefix
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_DCtx_refPrefix(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, const void* prefix, size_t prefixSize);
functions.description: References a single-use prefix (raw content by default) to decompress the next frame. The same prefix used during compression must be provided. Reference is discarded at end of frame (when ZSTD_decompressStream returns 0).
requirements: Adding any prefix (including NULL) invalidates any previously set prefix or dictionary.
Prefix buffer is referenced and must outlive decompression; it must remain unmodified until the frame ends (when ZSTD_decompressStream() returns 0).
Use ZSTD_isError() on the return value to detect errors.

data_types.description: A generic byte buffer with no required format or encoding. May contain any sequence of bytes including null bytes. Used here as raw input payloads to be compressed, decompressed, or interpreted as dictionary bytes or zstd frame data.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces arbitrary binary data suitable as:
# - raw payloads to compress (varied sizes and entropy)
# - dictionary bytes (with and without a Zstd dictionary header-like prefix)
# - already compressed-looking data chunks (for header parsing stubs)
# While inputs are arbitrary, we bias toward valid, compressible patterns, mixed with
# high-entropy segments, and sometimes embed plausible zstd frame headers to
# exercise header-parsing paths. Output size is capped <= 4096 bytes.

_MAX_BYTES = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _repeat_patterns(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Build compressible data by repeating chosen tokens with some randomness.
    out = bytearray()
    tokens: List[bytes] = []
    # Common compressible tokens
    base_tokens = [
        b"\x00" * 32,
        b"\xff" * 32,
        b"A" * 64,
        b"B" * 16,
        b"0123456789abcdef" * 4,
        b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, ",
    ]
    tokens.extend(base_tokens)
    # Add a few random short tokens
    for _ in range(4):
        tlen = rng.randint(1, 16)
        tokens.append(_rand_bytes(rng, tlen))
    # Generate repeats with occasional noise bursts
    while len(out) < length:
        t = rng.choice(tokens)
        reps = rng.randint(1, 10)
        chunk = (t * reps)[: max(1, rng.randint(8, 256))]
        out.extend(chunk)
        # Occasionally inject small random noise
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            noise_len = rng.randint(1, 32)
            out.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, noise_len))
    return bytes(out[:length])

def _high_entropy(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    return _rand_bytes(rng, length)

def _mixed_payload(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Blend compressible and random segments for realistic data.
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < length:
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            seg_len = rng.randint(16, 256)
            out.extend(_repeat_patterns(rng, seg_len))
        else:
            seg_len = rng.randint(8, 128)
            out.extend(_high_entropy(rng, seg_len))
    return bytes(out[:length])

def _maybe_zstd_frameish_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a plausible-looking zstd frame header to help header-parsing paths
    # Magic number 0xFD2FB528 (little-endian in file is 28 B5 2F FD)
    magic = b"\x28\xB5\x2F\xFD"
    # Build a minimal Frame Header Descriptor byte with reasonable flags.
    # For simplicity, choose a common pattern: content size present, single-segment.
    # FHD byte layout is complex; we only aim for plausibility for header readers.
    fhd = 0b00111000  # arbitrary plausible bits
    fhd_b = bytes([fhd])
    # Window descriptor or not depending on single-segment flag; we set single-segment so omit window
    # Content size: choose small size in VarInt (1 byte for small values 0..127)
    csize = rng.randint(0, 255)
    csize_enc = bytes([csize & 0xFF])
    # Dictionary ID flag off to avoid constraints
    # Header checksum disabled
    # This is not guaranteed to be a fully correct frame, but header-size readers may handle it.
    return magic + fhd_b + csize_enc

def _maybe_dict_header(rng: random.Random, body_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a plausible Zstd dictionary header: magic 0xEC30A437 (little-endian 37 A4 30 EC)
    magic = b"\x37\xA4\x30\xEC"
    # Dictionary ID (random 32-bit)
    dict_id = rng.getrandbits(32)
    # Some simple header fields (placeholder): 4 bytes for dict id, 4 bytes for params
    hdr = magic + struct.pack("<I", dict_id) + struct.pack("<I", rng.getrandbits(32))
    # Body of the dictionary
    body = _repeat_patterns(rng, body_len)
    return hdr + body

def _build_candidate_buffers(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    candidates: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Small highly compressible
    size1 = rng.randint(0, 256)  # allow empty, small
    candidates.append(_repeat_patterns(rng, size1))

    # 2) Medium mixed payload
    size2 = rng.randint(128, 1500)
    candidates.append(_mixed_payload(rng, size2))

    # 3) High-entropy chunk
    size3 = rng.randint(64, 1024)
    candidates.append(_high_entropy(rng, size3))

    # 4) Plausible zstd-frame-like header + payload trailer
    trailer_len = rng.randint(0, 256)
    candidates.append(_maybe_zstd_frameish_header(rng) + _mixed_payload(rng, trailer_len))

    # 5) Dictionary-like buffer (with header) of varied size
    body_len = rng.randint(32, 512)
    candidates.append(_maybe_dict_header(rng, body_len))

    # 6) Plain ASCII text paragraph to exercise dictionary-less, compressible input
    text_tokens = [
        b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. ",
        b"Zstandard is a real-time compression algorithm, providing high compression ratios. ",
        b"Data compression with dictionaries can greatly improve ratio on small payloads. ",
    ]
    paragraph = (rng.choice(text_tokens) * rng.randint(2, 8)) + (rng.choice(text_tokens) * rng.randint(1, 4))
    candidates.append(paragraph[: rng.randint(32, 1500)])

    # 7) Repeated numeric sequences
    nums = bytearray()
    for i in range(rng.randint(16, 256)):
        nums.extend(struct.pack("<I", rng.getrandbits(32)))
    candidates.append(bytes(nums[: rng.randint(32, len(nums))]))

    # 8) Short prefix buffers useful for refPrefix APIs
    prefix_len = rng.randint(1, 512)
    candidates.append(_mixed_payload(rng, prefix_len))

    return candidates

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of varied candidates
    cands = _build_candidate_buffers(rng)

    # Randomly select and possibly concatenate 1-3 candidates to provide
    # larger, still valid arbitrary data that can be used as src, dict, or frame bytes.
    pieces = rng.sample(cands, rng.randint(1, min(3, len(cands))))

    # Occasionally interleave small random paddings between pieces
    out = bytearray()
    for i, p in enumerate(pieces):
        out.extend(p)
        if i + 1 < len(pieces) and rng.random() < 0.4:
            pad_len = rng.randint(0, 32)
            out.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, pad_len))

    # Truncate to limit size
    if len(out) > _MAX_BYTES:
        out = out[:_MAX_BYTES]

    # Ensure non-empty to be useful for most stubs; if empty, add a small token
    if not out:
        out.extend(b"A")

    return bytes(out)
